Chapter 7: Navigating Triggers and Building Emotional Resilience
You know, even after months—or sometimes years—of making real progress, old wounds can still catch us off guard. Maybe it’s a phrase you haven’t heard in ages, a familiar scent, or even a sudden loud noise. Suddenly, your mind’s racing, you’re back in that painful memory, and it feels like the past is unfolding right in front of you. It’s jarring, isn’t it? One minute, everything feels steady... and the next, it’s as if you’ve lost your footing.
Take the story of a man who spent years feeling belittled at work. He thought he’d moved on, but during a simple performance review—where his boss was perfectly neutral—his whole body tensed up. Heart pounding, mind spinning with old fears. It took him a while to realize: his reaction wasn’t really about what was happening in that room. It was the echoes of the past coming back, uninvited.
And honestly, most of us don’t even notice how deeply triggers can shape our everyday lives. They sneak in anywhere—at home, at work, even when things are going well. Here’s something to pay attention to: the goal isn’t to avoid every trigger. It’s about learning how to respond with compassion and understanding, especially toward yourself.
Consider a woman who left a volatile relationship. Anytime someone raised their voice—whether in frustration or just excitement—she’d freeze up. At first, she blamed herself, thinking she was just “too sensitive.” But in time, she realized these reactions made sense. They were her body’s way of protecting her. She started practicing grounding techniques: deep breaths, tuning into her senses, reminding herself she was safe in this moment.
Building emotional resilience isn’t something that happens overnight. It’s a journey. It means learning to ride those emotional waves without letting them pull you under. For some, this looks like therapy or mindfulness. For others, it might be channeling energy into creative projects or getting active to shake off the tension.
I think of a teacher who survived a tough childhood. Every morning, she’d lace up her shoes and go running. With each stride, she felt her anxiety and stress melt away. The steady rhythm of her breath, the pounding of her feet... it became her meditation. A way to reconnect with her own strength.
It’s easy to feel defeated when those old triggers pop up, as if all your progress has vanished. But here’s the truth: every time you face a trigger and make it through, you’re growing just a little bit stronger. The fear may not vanish right away, but bit by bit, it becomes easier to handle.
Over time, you’ll notice the past starts to loosen its grip. Triggers show up less often, and when they do, they’re not quite as overwhelming. And you start to realize—you’ve survived this before. You know what to do. You’re not powerless.
